source: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 5 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 5
knowledgePattern: Minimise a quartic difference through its nonnegative squared input
solution:
The requirement is p(x)−q(x)=kx4−2x2+4k≥0 for every real x. Put u=x2, so every u≥0 is attainable. We require ku2−2u+4k≥0 on this half-line.

If k is negative, the value at u = 0 is negative. If k = 0, any positive u fails. Thus k must be positive.

For k>0, complete the square: ku2−2u+4k=k(u−1/k)2+4k−1/k. Its minimum occurs at the permitted input u=1/k. It is nonnegative exactly when 4k−1/k≥0, or 4k2≥1. With k positive this means k≥1/2.

Equality is allowed: at k = 1/2 the minimum is zero, not negative. This proves both necessity and sufficiency. Answer D.

hints.title: Subtract the two polynomials
hints.body: Subtract the two polynomials. Replace each x2 by u to get a quadratic in u.
hints.recap: Every allowed u must be nonnegative.
hints.pitfall: The inequality must work for every real x, not just one chosen x.
hints.pause: Simplify the quadratic and write its required range of u.

recall.reminder: Replacing a repeated square can reveal a quadratic.

hints.title: Sketch the quadratic for each sign of k
hints.body: Check k=0 first. Then sketch the quadratic for negative and positive k, using only u≥0.
hints.recap: The sign of the leading coefficient affects the graph’s shape.
hints.pitfall: Do not divide by k before checking whether k can be zero.
hints.pause: Decide which cases can stay nonnegative for every allowed u.

recall.reminder: Keep k fixed while checking every allowed input.

hints.title: Make the minimum nonnegative
hints.body: Complete the square in u. Check that the vertex lies in u≥0, then require the value there to be at least zero.
hints.recap: If the minimum is nonnegative, every other allowed value is too.
hints.pitfall: The question allows equality, so test the boundary value of k.
hints.pause: Solve the condition on k and check that it works for all u≥0.

recall.reminder: Completing the square shows a quadratic’s minimum.
